subject: Request: early termination & ramp protections — NimbusHealth (pilot)
messages:
From: Emma Lewis <emma@nimbushealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Early termination language + ramp concerns for pilot

Grace — thanks for the product walkthrough last week. Procurement has run our standard legal playbook and came back with two asks that will block signature unless we can address them: 1) an opt-out clause for early termination of the pilot with a 30-day notice and full refund pro-rata; 2) an explicit ramp schedule tied to MRR thresholds so our finance team can justify spend reductions after month 3.

We understand Redwood's default is not to allow refunds for committed ramp, but given this is a 3-month paid pilot with sensitive PHI workloads (HIPAA), they want a clear safety valve. Can you confirm whether Redwood can offer any downsell protections (partial refund cap or reduced commitments) and whether the ramp schedule can be softened?

We're trying to keep this simple — if you can provide proposed language and run it past your deal desk/execs ASAP, we can keep the signature timeline this week.

Thanks,
Emma Lewis
Director, Procurement — NimbusHealth
(Attachment: Nimbus-PO-Intent.pdf)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lewis <emma@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Early termination language + ramp concerns for pilot

Emma — appreciate the clear ask. I've looped in Rishi and Marcus to escalate for deal-desk / exec approval. Quick summary of what we can consider:

- Offer a tiered ramp schedule tied to usage bands (0-50% expected baseline, 51-90% partial ramp, 91-100% full ramp) with month-to-month opt-outs after month 2 if usage remains under 50%.
- Limited early termination refund: cap refunds at the greater of 25% of remaining committed value or $10k, whichever is lower, to balance customer protection with our capacity reservation costs.
- Require 30 days' notice for opt-out and that any PHI-specific enablement work is non-refundable.

I'll escalate a redline with the suggested wording and ask for expedited exec sign-off. If you can confirm Nimbus' preferred refund cap (percentage vs fixed cap) we can tailor.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Grace's thread. Quick background: 3-month pilot, potential to expand into a 12–24 month enterprise contract. Customer is firm on some opt-out language for pilot given PHI. Grace proposes a compromise; below are my suggested approvals and constraints:

- Approve a partial refund equal to 25% of unused committed value or $10k cap (whichever is lower) for early termination during the pilot only.
- Ramp schedule: include explicit usage bands and automatic step-down pricing if usage stays below 50% for two consecutive weeks after month 1.
- Require that any infra prep (HIPAA config, dedicated routing) is billable and non-refundable.
- Approval contingent on Sales Ops recording a Revised Commitment and Legal approving the redline.

I'm ok to approve this as a one-time concession to close the pilot. If approved, will we mark the concession as "pilot-only" in the contract and attach a follow-up renewal pricing guardrail?

—Rishi
Head of Sales Strategy — Redwood Inference

Rishi / Lauren — I agree with the concession for this pilot but want to ensure we don't set a precedent that bleeds into enterprise deals. Specific asks from my side:

1) Refund cap: prefer a fixed cap ($10k) rather than percentage to keep accounting predictable.
2) Add a clause: refunds only applicable if Redwood has confirmed capacity allocation tied to the pilot (so we can bill for reserved instances).
3) Replace "2 consecutive weeks" trigger with "two consecutive 30-day reporting periods" to avoid micro-fluctuation gaming.

If Legal OKs the redline with those edits, I'm comfortable signing off from a revenue-impact perspective. Grace — ask Emma if Nimbus can accept the $10k cap and the longer reporting period; if not, we'll need to review discount trade-offs (e.g., additional seat credits vs larger refund).
